summary:
AtrodKids: A Space Adventure for Learning Through Play
Our project involves the development of an educational Q&A-style video game featuring Roby, a robot that guides players on a space exploration adventure. Through an interactive quiz, children aged 6 and 7 can learn about the equipment and devices left behind by NASA on the Moon and Mars following their missions, as well as discover interesting facts about explorations conducted by the International Space Station (ISS).
To develop the game, we researched space-related information, designed the settings and characters, programmed the interactive elements, incorporated music and sound effects, integrated all the components, and finally published our video game.
The challenge is addressed through creativity, research, logical thinking, and programming, combining both technological and scientific knowledge.
The significance of this project lies in bringing science and space exploration closer to young children in a fun, dynamic, and interactive way, transforming learning into a gaming experience. Our goal is to provide a digital educational resource that sparks curiosity, fosters an interest in science, and enables learning through play.
details:
ASTRODKIDS: Learning Through Space Exploration

AstrodKids is an educational and interactive video game designed for children ages 6 and 7. Its main character is Roby, a friendly robot who guides players through a space exploration quiz featuring questions and answers.

The game encourages children to discover and learn about the equipment, devices, and technologies that NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars after completing some of its missions, as well as the explorations and activities carried out aboard the International Space Station (ISS).

How does it work?

Roby asks questions related to the topics researched, and players must select the correct answers to progress through the game. Through space-themed settings, characters, interactive objects, music, and programming, the game creates a digital adventure that combines entertainment and learning.

How did we develop the project?

The development process was organized into six stages:

  1. Research: We gathered information about the equipment and devices NASA left on the Moon and Mars, as well as the explorations conducted aboard the ISS.
  2. Design: We created the backgrounds, characters, and objects featured in the video game.
  3. Programming: We developed the interactions, questions, answers, and movements of the different game elements.
  4. Music and Sound: We added music and sound effects to enhance the player's experience.
  5. Integration: We combined and connected all the programming elements to ensure the complete game functioned properly.
  6. Publication: We published and shared our game so other children could access it and learn while playing.

What benefits does it offer, and what impact do we hope to achieve?

AstrodKids aims to bring science, technology, and space exploration closer to young children through a fun and accessible learning experience. It encourages curiosity, memory, the understanding of new concepts, decision-making, and logical thinking. It also promotes independent learning and interest in space missions.

What tools and resources did we use?

To develop the project, we used digital design and programming tools to create the settings, characters, objects, sounds, and different game interactions. Programming allowed us to bring Roby to life and connect all the elements to build an interactive experience.

What makes our project creative?

The creativity behind AstrodKids lies in transforming scientific and technological information about real space missions into an educational video game specially designed for young children. Roby is more than just a character: he is a guide who turns learning content into challenges, questions, and discoveries.

What factors did we consider?

We mainly considered the age of our target audience. We used simple language, friendly characters, attractive visuals, age-appropriate questions, and an easy-to-use game design. We also focused on making the information interesting, keeping the game entertaining, and ensuring that each stage offered a new learning opportunity.

Our goal is for AstrodKids to become a digital educational tool that invites children to become little space explorers, demonstrating that technology and programming can also open the door to scientific knowledge.
